title: E3 Ubiquitin Ligase CHIP Inhibits Haemocyte Proliferation and Differentiation via the Ubiquitination of Runx in the Pacific Oyster.
authors: Dong, Miren; Song, Ying; Wang, Weilin; Song, Xiaorui; Wu, Wei; Wang, Lingling; Song, Linsheng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究牡蛎中E3泛素连接酶CHIP通过泛素化转录因子Runx调控血细胞增殖分化，涉及蛋白-DNA互作（Runx与DNA结合）及分子对接方法，但核心是免疫细胞调控而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，方法深度有限。
abstract: Mollusca first evolve primitive immune cells (namely, haemocytes), which assemble a notable complex innate immune system, which are continuously produced through proliferation and differentiation and infused in the haemolymph. As a typical E3 ligase, CHIP is critical for immune cell turnover and homeostasis in vertebrates. In this study, a CHIP homolog (CgCHIP) with a high expression in haemocytes was identified in oysters to investigate its role in the proliferation and differentiation of ancient innate immune cells. CgCHIP exhibited a widespread distribution across all haemocyte subpopulations, and the knockdown of CgCHIP altered the composition of haemocytes as examined by flow cytometry. Mechanistically screened with bioinformatics and immunoprecipitation, a key haematopoietic transcription factor CgRunx was identified as a substrate of CgCHIP. Moreover, amino acids in the interacted intervals of CgCHIP and CgRunx were determined by molecular docking. Experimental evidence from an in vitro culture model of an agranulocyte subpopulation and an in vivo oyster model revealed that the knockdown of CgCHIP and CgRunx had opposing effects on agranulocyte (precursor cells) differentiation and granulocyte (effector cells) proliferation. In summary, CgCHIP negatively regulated agranulocyte differentiation and granulocyte proliferation by mediating the ubiquitination and degradation of CgRunx in oysters. These results offer insight into the involvement of ubiquitylation in controlling haemocyte turnover in primitive invertebrates.
abstract_zh: 软体动物首次演化出原始免疫细胞（即血细胞），这些细胞组装成一个显著复杂的先天免疫系统，通过增殖和分化持续产生，并注入血淋巴中。作为一种典型的E3连接酶，CHIP在脊椎动物的免疫细胞更新和稳态维持中至关重要。本研究在牡蛎中鉴定出一个CHIP同源物（CgCHIP），其在血细胞中高表达，旨在探讨其在古老先天免疫细胞增殖和分化中的作用。CgCHIP在所有血细胞亚群中广泛分布，且敲低CgCHIP通过流式细胞术检测改变了血细胞的组成。通过生物信息学和免疫沉淀的机制筛选，鉴定出关键造血转录因子CgRunx为CgCHIP的底物。此外，通过分子对接确定了CgCHIP和CgRunx相互作用区间内的氨基酸。来自无颗粒细胞亚群体外培养模型和体内牡蛎模型的实验证据表明，敲低CgCHIP和CgRunx对无颗粒细胞（前体细胞）分化和颗粒细胞（效应细胞）增殖具有相反的影响。总之，CgCHIP通过介导CgRunx的泛素化和降解，负调控牡蛎中无颗粒细胞分化和颗粒细胞增殖。这些结果为泛素化在控制原始无脊椎动物血细胞更新中的作用提供了见解。
